analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Bounce; Wise mixed; Credit debate; Indian IT services; EU satelite fast track; Google Quantum; Informa cancels event
key_insights: US trading stayed volatile. The S&P 500 finished higher and the Nasdaq 100 was nearly flat after an early Tech/AI sell-off and heavy long-only semiconductor selling. Investors rotated into Mag 7, Staples, MedTech, Tools and Financials, and small caps outperformed (RTY > SPX > NDX).
Long-only flows improved from 40% better for sale in the morning to 25% at the close, driven by tech supply against demand for Financials and Healthcare. Hedge funds finished only 3% better for sale.

The Nasdaq recovered its 50- and 100-day moving averages, but sentiment is weak. GS TMT Momentum Pairs fell about 12% in two days and semiconductors have declined seven consecutive sessions. GS attributes this to the unwind of the long-AI/short-bonds trade, rising credit concerns, and uncertainty around earnings, elections, rates, inflation, ROIC and product momentum.
CoreWeave bounced 6% after the prior day's focus and its CDS stopped moving out. GS has received many questions on how to think about it.

US Prime data shows TMT-focused funds down 2.0% (-1.4 SD), down 4.7% over two sessions, and still up 14.8% YTD. Hedge funds net sold Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI) for five consecutive sessions (Oct 8-14), reversing all cumulative net buying in the group since the start of 2025. The European Prime Book shows semis ownership still relatively high and little change in software.

GS credit research (Amanda) says concerns over financing the AI capex buildout are raising the cost of capital for weaker borrowers. USD high-yield AI spreads widened 25bp to 360bp over Treasuries on 13-14 October versus 2bp for non-AI issuers. The pressure is concentrated in neoclouds, frontier-lab-exposed companies and data-centre project finance, while diversified energy and utility names were more resilient.

Investment-grade AI spreads moved only modestly wider, but dispersion is rising as investors reassess off-taker risk, higher-for-longer rates and energy costs. Project-finance issuance has exceeded $106B this year, nearly three times 2025's total, with a forecast of $300B in 2027 plus a projected $420B of direct hyperscaler issuance. The team is underweight USD IG Technology and neutral USD HY after the sell-off, and argues for a deal-by-deal approach.

Wise delivered 2QFY27 transaction revenue growth of about 21% YoY ex-FX and net revenue growth of about 20%, modestly ahead of expectations. FY27 net revenue guidance was raised to the upper half of the 15-20% medium-term range (17.5-20%). GS raised its FY27 net revenue growth estimate to 19.7% from 17.9% but cut its FY27 PBT margin estimate to 25.0% from 26.2% on higher one-offs and investment. 1HFY27 IBT margin is guided to about 23%, including about 2ppts of one-offs. GS stays Buy. There is no update on the Brussels case, and Platform is now over 6% of volumes.

Indian IT services reported a better-than-expected quarter. Tech Mahindra's revenue growth beat by about 90bps and is running roughly twice as fast as large-cap peers. Wipro beat on growth and margins, but its trailing-12-month deal wins fell 26% YoY. GS says AI-related deflation is not yet large enough to cause an outright revenue decline, so terminal-value concerns may be overdone. The sector remains in low-single-digit growth. Estimates rise modestly for Tech Mahindra and Wipro, and both stay Sell.

Microsoft preview: shares are up 38% since July. Focus is AI monetisation and capex returns, with potential upside from Azure growth of 46-47% versus 44-45% guidance, Copilot and agent adoption, and M365 Commercial Cloud growth of 17-18%. Recent management commentary suggests greater capex flexibility, and Maia chips should support margins over time.

EU may fast-track Project Bromo (the Airbus-Leonardo-Thales satellite JV), a SpaceX rival, for Phase 1 approval (Bloomberg). The Commission has spent more than a year on antitrust concerns, and clearance may still require concessions.

Google says it demonstrated 'magic state cultivation' on its Willow processor, cutting errors about 40x and reaching 99.99% logical fidelity. Magic states can consume up to 95% of system capacity, so the result could reduce the qubits, cryogenic infrastructure and capital needed for a commercial machine. Google still has to show the technique works at much larger scale.

Memory: CXMT's 4F2 announcement triggered an 11-26% sell-off across major memory stocks and erased over $700B of market value. Weakness in CXMT itself and in NAND names suggests AI-financing, credit and inflation concerns also contributed. Meaningful gaps remain for CXMT in customer qualification, high-yield production, advanced-node DRAM and HBM versus Samsung and SK Hynix. Korean memory leaders trade below book value on 2027-28 estimates, so the correction may be pricing an overly bearish downcycle.

Besi/ASML: SemiAnalysis argues ASML could enter die-to-wafer hybrid bonding and challenge Besi. Two other brokers have downgraded Besi on the same concerns, and on concerns that hybrid bonding adoption in HBM is running later than expected. No product has been announced. The GS author thinks the thesis is increasingly consensus and likely right.

Samsung will start construction of its second Taylor plant next month, and the first Taylor fab is on track to be online by end of this year. Samsung also scaled back Q4 mid-to-low-end smartphone production because of glass fabric price hikes for CCL and surging memory prices that squeezed margins.

MediaTek is reportedly in final-stage talks for ByteDance's AI ASIC orders, which would add a second major customer after Google. The deal is unconfirmed. Micron's new Taichung advanced packaging and testing facility reportedly has 2027 capacity fully booked.

Meta launched an open-weight model, Muse Spark Open (816B parameters, 1M token context), that runs on Macs. Amazon devices chief Panos Panay described ambient AI devices replacing apps, and Amazon unveiled two Bee-brand wearables (Frontier bracelet, Eclipse brick).

Ericsson: GS calls the move a short squeeze plus an Asian pull-forward of purchases ahead of expected price increases. Management said the pull-forward was not large enough to distort the 2027 outlook. The numbers were better than expected, but the stock is not cheap for the growth and GS sees it drifting back a little. Management said AI-driven component inflation is structural and cannot be absorbed indefinitely. It has protected margins so far through substitution, upselling, mix and licensing.

Informa cancelled the Global Health Expo 2026 in Riyadh (26-29 Oct) and moved it to October 2027. The event is about 3% of exhibitors and attendees across its Top 50 events and an estimated 0.5% of 2026 group revenue. Cityscape Saudi is still scheduled for mid-November.

Telefonica is considering a vendor loan to help the Oxio-led Melisa consortium complete its $450M purchase of Movistar Mexico. DB upgraded Telia to Buy. The UK DCMS issued a notice of potential intervention in the Sky-ITV deal citing four public-interest considerations under the Enterprise Act 2002.

Positioning is cleaner but not fully washed out. The GS sentiment indicator has been negative for six weeks, and the Global AI basket had its second-largest net selling day of the past year. Net allocation fell to 26.1% from 31.7% in June and the long/short ratio to 3.27 from 4.34. Skew and short-dated vol were sold as spot stabilised, while RUT vol was bid further out the curve.

tension_points.bull_case: The buildout is hard to derail because AI demand continues to exceed supply, and investment-grade AI spreads moved only modestly wider on stronger balance sheets.
tension_points.bear_case: High-yield AI spreads widened 25bp versus 2bp for non-AI issuers, concentrated in neoclouds, frontier-lab-exposed companies and data-centre project finance, on off-taker risk, higher-for-longer rates and energy costs.

tension_points.bull_case: Korean memory leaders trade below book value on 2027-28 estimates, so the correction may be pricing an overly bearish downcycle.
tension_points.bear_case: CXMT is making real progress in DRAM capacity, with a planned 4F2 server DRAM launch by end-2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gaps remain for CXMT in customer qualification, high-yield production, advanced-node DRAM and HBM, which would limit the threat.
